messages:
zoe: Heads-up — since ~03:42 UTC we've seen a big spike in SCIM 403s from the IdP. Root error in provisioning-service logs: 'signature verification failed' and repeated KMS decrypt errors when handling inbound SCIM payloads. Anyone seeing related alerts?

raj: I see it. provisioning-service shows repeated `KMSDecryptionException: failed to unwrap key` starting 03:41:56. idp-proxy logs show `401 invalid_jwt` around the same time.

amelia: Did the IdP rotate JWKS/certs? `kid` mismatches are classic for this. @zoe can you paste the IdP `.well-known/jwks.json` or a snippet and any cached jwk fingerprints we have?

zoe: Pulled the jwks — it contains new kid `k-2026-03` and the older `k-2025-12` is still present. Our auth-cacher log shows we fetched the new jwks but then later `mapped_kid=null` for many tokens. Example: `auth-cacher: WARN verifyToken: no matching kid for token kid=k-2026-03`

mike: The KMSDecryptionException is worrying too — are SCIM bodies envelope-encrypted and wrapped with a DEK that we unwrap with CMK? If the CMK was rotated the DEK unwrap would fail. Check the `KMS_ALIAS` env for provisioning pods.

raj: Confirmed env: `KMS_ALIAS=arn:aws:kms:us-west-2:123:alias/redwood-provisioning` (unchanged). But AWS CloudTrail shows `InvalidCiphertextException` for decrypt requests from the provisioning-service principal at 03:41:56. That smells like the alias now points to a different key id.

amelia: Right — if alias was updated to a new CMK, old DEKs wrapped under the previous key id can't be unwrapped by the new key. We need to check the alias -> key mapping.

zoe: Ran `aws kms list-aliases --query "Aliases[?AliasName=='alias/redwood-provisioning']"` — alias now points to key id `key-ef12`. Previously it was `key-ab34`. Looks like a CMK rotation happened and the alias was switched. That explains the KMS errors for queued payloads encrypted under the old key.

mike: So two independent rotations overlapped: IdP rotated jwks/certs (JWTs failing), and we rotated KMS alias (DEKs failing). Combined effect: SCIM requests failing with 401/403 and internal KMS unwrap failures. Oof.

security-bot: :rotating_light: Alert: SSO_PROVISIONING_ERROR spike (700%) — auto-created incident INC-2026-111.

raj: Short-term mitigations proposal: 1) restore alias to previous key id so queued payloads can be unwrapped; 2) restart auth-cacher to force a fresh jwks fetch and clear stale kid mappings; 3) pause SCIM sync to avoid noisy retries and more failures until backlog drained. @mike can you flip the alias back?

mike: On it. Running: `aws kms update-alias --alias-name alias/redwood-provisioning --target-key-id key-ab34` (rolling alias back to previous key id).

mike: Done. I can see provisioning-service logs showing fewer KMS errors now. Restarting auth-cacher to pick up jwks and remap kids. Command: `kubectl rollout restart deploy/auth-cacher -n prod`

zoe: Restarted auth-cacher. After restart, JWKS mapping appears fixed and SCIM responses are returning 200 for previously failing requests. Paused SCIM sync for 10m to let backlog drain.

amelia: Postmortem owners/measures: I'll take the write-up. Immediate action items: (a) document a CMK rotation playbook including safe alias swap and DEK rewrap strategy, (b) implement a DEK rewrap job that attempts decrypt+rewrap for stored DEKs when alias changes, (c) add pre-rotation checks (service principals IAM permissions on new key, test decrypt of a sample DEK), (d) require scheduled maintenance windows for IdP jwks/cert rotations when possible.

mike: I'll add terraform guardrails to prevent accidental alias re-pointing without a rollout flag and create a quick runbook for alias rollback.

zoe: Thanks all — marking incident INC-2026-111 as 'triaged'. Will close after backlog fully drains and we've verified no further 403s. I'll link the postmortem to the incident and a follow-up PM ticket.
